Eve (Support): FYI - Customer ACME reported function-calling returning the wrong tool repeatedly. They expected route_planner but model keeps selecting geocode. Escalating because it causes billing spikes and bad UX. Logs attached below.
Rajat (Eng-runtime): Can you paste the exact request payload + the model reply? Need to confirm whether tool_choice is coming from the model or our router.
Eve (Support): Pasting sanitized request: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Plan a 3-stop delivery route from SFO to Palo Alto, avoid tolls"}],
  "functions": [
    {"name":"route_planner", "description":"Compute multi-stop driving routes with constraints", "parameters": {...}
    },
    {"name":"geocode", "description":"Return lat/long for a given address", "parameters": {...}
    }
  ]
}```
Eve (Support): Model reply we received (truncated): ```json
{
  "id": "resp_abc",
  "choices": [
    {"message": {"role":"assistant","content": null,"function_call": {"name": "geocode", "arguments": "{\"address\": \"SFO\"}"}}}
  ]
}```
Marta (ML): Hmm looks like model selected geocode for the first step (identify coords) instead of invoking route_planner which we want to handle sequencing. Could be ambiguity in function naming or our schema not sufficiently constraining. Do we surface function metadata to model in the same order every time?
Eve (Support): Customer says it happens ~30% of the time and bloats token usage because we then call route_planner after geocode, doubling calls. Billing impact reported.
Jules (SRE): ops-bot flagged rate uptick and we throttled calls per-account, but that only helps cost, not correctness.
Rajat (Eng-runtime): Check 3 things: 1) Are we sending the full functions[].description field? 2) Is our function schema for route_planner specifying required top-level fields so model is more likely to pick it? 3) Is there a router policy that remaps function names?
Eve (Support): Confirmed we send descriptions. Example snippet from our request log: ```json
"functions": [{"name":"route_planner","description":"Compute multi-stop driving routes with constraints (avoid tolls, optimize time)","parameters":{"type":"object"}}, {"name":"geocode","description":"Lookup latitude/longitude for an address","parameters":{"type":"object"}}]
```
Marta (ML): Two likely causes: (A) model heuristics think geocode is the first logical call (get coords) vs route_planner which expects coords, or (B) function descriptions are too similar / no examples provided. We can try: add explicit sample function_call examples in system prompt or reorder functions so route_planner appears first. Also consider adding a top-level function alias like "route_planner.compute_route" to reduce ambiguity.
Rajat (Eng-runtime): Reordering functions is a cheap experiment. We should also add a post-processing check in router: if model calls geocode but user intent mentions "plan route" -> auto-suggest invoking route_planner instead of following up with additional calls. That reduces double-call pattern.
Eve (Support): Customer wants a fix w/in 48h. They offered access to a sample prompt and full logs. I attached link: https://acme.example.com/incident/6421 (internal).
Jules (SRE): Action: throttle won't fix correctness. I'll whitelist ACME for a dedicated rate-limit to avoid interrupted playback while we test.
Rajat (Eng-runtime): I'll run two repros: (1) send functions[] as-is, (2) reorder functions with route_planner first, (3) augment system prompt with a short instruction: "If user asks to plan a route, prefer route_planner; only call geocode when address-only resolution explicitly requested. Provide example function_call format."
Marta (ML): Also try naming: change geocode -> address_lookup temporarily to see if name similarity was the issue. We'll also add a toy few-shot example into messages showing route_planner used directly.
Eve (Support): Quick repro steps for the env: curl to our /v1/chat/completions with same body, customer uses model redwood-chat-1. They reproduce locally.
Rajat (Eng-runtime): ETA: 6-8 hours for initial experiments. If we can reduce model-level misrouting to <5% we'll recommend a rollout path. If not, we need infra-level policy to override model choice via intent heuristics.
Marta (ML): If we add examples, watch for overfitting—ensure we don't bias model to always call route_planner when user only wants a lat/long. We'll add an explicit negative example too.
Eve (Support): Customer asked for interim mitigation: can you add a temporary router rule that downgrades geocode calls to a delayed fallback (i.e., attempt route_planner first)?
Rajat (Eng-runtime): Yes. I'll add a canary rule for ACME that checks the user query for route-planning keywords and suppresses immediate geocode invocation.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-6421, owner @Rajat. Priority: P2.
Eve (Support): Thanks. I'll update the customer with repro schedule and patch plan. Adding owner to thread: @Rajat. :thumbsup:
Marta (ML): I'll post experiment results in this thread.
Rajat (Eng-runtime): Will do. If anyone else sees similar misroutes, please drop examples here so we can cluster.
Eve (Support): Closing loop: customer happy with canary plan for now, still expects permanent fix. Will follow-up after test. :white_check_mark:
